items.text: Does a validated GPU spectral turbulence simulation on one rented 8-GPU node show cost per large-eddy turnover rising with Reynolds number, as the claimed Re³ law predicts?
Cost per large-eddy turnover will scale roughly as N⁴, i.e. Rλ⁶, so 100× compute buys only about 2.15× in Rλ [wiki_dns].

sources.quote: the number of operations grows as Re³

items.text: Time stepping: about 50,280 sequential steps at 1024³, each depending on the previous one.
Each 3D FFT is split across 8 GPUs in slabs, with an NCCL all-to-all transpose, so the transforms within one time step run in parallel.
Fitted exponents near a≈2/3 (Rλ∝N^a), b≈4 (dollars per T_L∝N^b), c≈6 (∝Rλ^c): extra compute buys little Reynolds number.
Fitted exponents differ clearly from 2/3, 4 and 6 with confidence intervals excluding them, e.g. because u′ and ε do not stay fixed across rungs.

Build a GPU spectral turbulence solver, check it against the public JHTDB 1024³ run (Rλ 418), then run a 128³ to 1024³ ladder on rented H100 nodes to measure how dollars per turnover grow with Rλ, comparing with the Re³ law [wiki_dns].

items.text: JHTDB isotropic1024 is a published 1024³ pseudo-spectral DNS at Rλ 418 with stored fields; Wikipedia states DNS operations grow as Re³. Neither gives measured dollars per turnover on rented GPUs.
A measured dollars-versus-Rλ curve on rented hardware, with fitted exponents and an open validated solver, is not given by the cited sources.
Reproduce JHTDB isotropic1024 time-averaged Rλ of 418 with our 1024³ solver [jhtdb_readme]

Cost per step is only bandwidth arithmetic until the bake-off measures it. Only one node and one forcing scheme; JHTDB scheme details may leave a mismatch floor. JHTDB cutout access was unconfirmed (HTTP 503).

items.text: With data held fixed, does more fine-tuning compute raise task success of a small robot vision-language-action model in simulation, or does data limit it?
At fixed data, 15k to 50k steps shifts success under 3 points; more data adds 10 or more points [arXiv 2506.01844].
At fixed data, 15k to 50k steps (3.3x compute) raises average success by 3 points or more, so compute still buys success.
At each data level, 15k to 50k steps moves success under 3 points; at 50k steps, 100% data beats 25% by 10 or more points.

Fine-tune SmolVLA on LIBERO in 25 runs, varying steps (5k, 15k, 50k) and data (10 to 100%) independently, plus capacity, camera removal and pretraining arms. Score 27 checkpoints on 2,000 rollouts each against a published 87.3% baseline.
SmolVLA paper reports LIBERO results at 0.24B/0.45B/2.25B sizes and says it can train for far fewer steps without significant loss, but gives no step or data grid [smolvla_paper].

scores.reason: Root question is about robot hands; DNS cost scaling for turbulence bears on no robot-manipulation choice, and Re³ is already well known.
Compute axis spans 8x in N (about 4000x cost) and held_fixed is good, but exponent fits on four rungs may not separate cleanly; noise treatment is loose.
Scored against published JHTDB Rλ 418 with stated tolerances, reproduced first; the truth is independent of the method under test.
Re³ scaling is textbook and already answers the scaling question; only dollars on rented GPUs is new, and the plan states that gap.
Slab-split FFTs parallelise only within each time step; the 50,280 sequential steps stay in order.
Baseline copies are none and single-GPU baseline is not tuned or timed to one answer; anchor checks against published values, not a sequential run.

critique.decides_by_reason: Exponents are fitted only after the ladder and the 1024³ run (P6). No earlier phase lets decision_rule be applied for either outcome.

scores.reason: Result bears on scale-vs-collect choice only via a small simulated model, one family, in-distribution; no touch or real-robot step checked.
Steps span 10x and are held fixed well, noise is stated, but 15k to 50k is 3.3x and data varies jointly; the 3-point threshold sits near the 2.1-point noise.
Exact simulator success flags, with a harness gate reproducing the published pi0.5 97.5% within a stated tolerance before training.
Prior gives sizes and says fewer steps suffice, but no step-by-data grid; the plan states the gap. Partial overlap on the steps claim.
Runs are independent copies one per GPU; training steps stay sequential and method is none, so no dependency is removed.
restructuring.method is none, so the baseline criterion does not apply.

critique.decides_by_reason: Decision rule needs 15k and 50k scores, which only wave1 produces for the first cells; the pilot only gates the harness. Earliest sufficient phase is wave1.
